ledger.claim: The rider filed this dispute and the fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the present state is that the rider has paid the full SGD 12.87. Under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION ruling on a rider-filed dispute leaves that charge exactly where it is; only a refund moves the rider off the disputed charge. The question for the tribunal is therefore whether the disputed SGD 12.87 stays with the rider or comes back.

The platform's own booking estimate for this trip is 2.5 km over 8.0 minutes (POL-RD-01 makes optimal_distance_km the platform route estimate stored on the trip record at booking). The platform's own trace of the route actually driven measures 5.5 km. The excess is therefore 3.0 km. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass: 3.0 km is 120% of the 2.5 km optimal, above the 20% test, and 3.0 km absolute is far above the 0.8 km test. A route deviation is established.

POL-RD-01 provides that where the trace figure and the trip record's actual_distance_km disagree, gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs and actual_distance_km may not be cited for the threshold test. Here the two agree at 5.5 km, so the finding is safe on either field; the trace figure is a measured spherical polyline length over 90 fixes at 100% coverage, not a rounded convenience copy, and it is the figure the threshold finding rests on.

The excess of 3.0 km is 120% of the optimal distance, which is above the 50% of optimal_distance_km materiality threshold, so this is additionally a MATERIAL deviation under POL-RD-01, not a marginal one. The 8.0 km absolute materiality limb is not reached, but the percentage limb is, and it is sufficient on its own.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes, so no independent corroboration is needed. POL-RD-07(a) to (c) sets the policy-level limits at a gap over 90 seconds between consecutive fixes, a straight-line jump over 500 m, or a sustained sampling interval over 30 seconds. This trace carries 90 fixes at a 10-second sample interval matching the 10-second expected interval, 100% coverage, no gaps at all and a maximum gap of 10 seconds. The rider's deviation therefore rests on a clean trace, and the POL-RD-07(ii) corroboration requirement and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation are not engaged.

The rider did ask, in the chat log, to stop at Golden Mile Tower first (MSG-00805-001, sent 13:59:40, before the vehicle moved at 14:00:00), and the driver replied 'I see your message'. But the driver's admitted reason for the route fails its own corroboration test. POL-RD-04 requires the trace to show the vehicle passing within 200 m of the requested waypoint, and the platform's waypoint match on this trace shows the nearest fix was 1592 m from the waypoint hint coordinate - nearly eight times the radius the clause sets. Under POL-RD-14 the instruction therefore did not cause the measured excess: no distance is excluded from the excess, and the deviation is decided on the trace as measured.

No traffic advisory covers this trip. The bundle's advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-00805-01 is MISSING: it carries no payload, status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, and the trace's advisory-area block returns an empty advisory list. That artifact is disclosed as impaired and is cited only for its absence. Because no advisory on file names any road the optimal route traverses, the POL-RD-03 external-cause comparison cannot be run and no closure exoneration is available to the driver. If any traffic cause is read into the driver's statement, POL-RD-13 makes an assertion of that kind weightless where no advisory is on file, and the deviation stands at the measured figure.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. Limb (a): trip id TRP-00805 is common to the trip record, the gps trace and the fare breakdown, and no timestamp across the admitted artifacts runs backwards or disagrees by more than 10 minutes, so nothing here reaches the POL-RD-10(4) escalation trigger. Limb (b): the excess of 3.0 km meets the POL-RD-01 threshold and is measured from a trace that is not impaired under POL-RD-07. The burden has shifted to the driver, and the only artifact he points to - the chat request - fails its own corroboration test under POL-RD-14.

The additional corroboration hurdle POL-RD-08 imposes on a claim with excess below 30% does not apply here: it operates only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more, and the rider's trailing-60-day figures are 0 claims and 0 substantiated. No extra corroboration beyond the trace is required of this rider, and this factor cannot be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven.

The upfront-quote route out of the refund is closed on this record. The fare breakdown records fare_model METERED and quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not run and the distance-and-time charges were not fixed at booking. POL-RD-02 therefore governs the remedy on this trip.

The refund under POL-RD-02 is arithmetic. Recomputed fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 2.5 optimal km + 0.28 x 8.0 optimal min) x 1.0 surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + no ERP or tolls on the optimal route + 0.00 waiting time fee - 0.00 promo = 8.715. Charged total is 12.87, so the refund is 4.155 before rounding, 32.3% of the charged total. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so the outcome is not NO_ACTION, and it is far below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 4.20, the payable figure rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05.

No pass-through line needs to be added on top of the POL-RD-02 refund, and none may be double-counted. The fare breakdown charges no ERP at all - erp_gantries is empty and the off-optimal-route ERP total is SGD 0.00 - and it carries no airport surcharge, which is correct because this trip neither originates nor ends at an airport. There is accordingly no off-route gantry to itemise and no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09; the refund is confined to the distance-and-time lines computed above, exactly as POL-RD-09(1) requires.

The rider asks the tribunal to 'review the whole fare', but the most this case can move is the arithmetic of POL-RD-02, and that arithmetic caps the refund well below the contested 12.87. On EV-FARE-00805 the charged total is 12.87; recomputed against the booked optimal of 2.5 km and 8.0 minutes, ((3.80 + 0.75 x 2.5 + 0.28 x 8.0) x surge 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP and tolls + 0 fixed surcharges + 0 waiting time - 0 promo gives a recomputed fare of 8.715, a refund before rounding of 4.155, and a payable figure of 4.20. That is 32.3% of the charge, far below the 90% share that POL-RD-02 requires before a FULL_REFUND replaces the partial. The rider's exposure is therefore capped at 4.20 and the claim for the entire fare cannot succeed.

The material deviation on this trip triggers the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check, and that check comes back negative on the clause's own test. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 300, so neither limb of the pattern test is satisfied: there is no count of 3 or more, and the ratio is 0.000 against the 0.05 threshold with well over 40 trips in the window. It follows that the rider cannot obtain the FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b), and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) is warranted. Under POL-GEN-01 no other profile field may be used for this test, including the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter, which is not the trailing-90-day figure the clause names.

ledger.claim: No pass-through line enlarges the rider's position on this trip. EV-FARE-00805 carries no ERP gantry and no airport surcharge - erp_lines total is 0.00 and the trip ends at, rather than originates at, an airport, so the airport surcharge in the fare model is not chargeable and no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity correction exists. A POL-RD-09 pass-through correction therefore adds nothing to the rider, and under POL-RD-09(1) no off-route ERP amount may be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. The total movement on this case stays at the single recomputed refund of 4.20 and nothing more.

The rider's own message is on the record and it is the reason this route is not a driver's invention: sent at 13:59:40 by the rider and read 20 seconds before the vehicle moved off, it asks the driver to 'stop at Golden Mile Tower first' and carries a waypoint hint. That satisfies POL-RD-04(a), (b) and (c) - it is the rider's instruction, it predates departure, and it names a place specifically. The corroboration limb, however, cannot be met on this trace, and the driver does not ask the tribunal to pretend otherwise: the nearest fix to the requested waypoint is 1,592.1 m, far outside the 200 m threshold POL-RD-04 sets, so no distance is excluded and no amended optimal is supplied. POL-RD-14 is explicit that this is a failed corroboration, not the mutually contradictory evidence described in POL-RD-10(7); the driver's reliance on the request is an explanation that the trace does not carry, not evidence of comparable strength against the trace.

This case is fully decidable on the bundle and does not meet any escalation trigger, so the disputed amount should be resolved by a monetary ruling rather than held. The trip identifier matches across EV-TRIP-00805, EV-GPS-00805 and EV-FARE-00805 and the timestamps are consistent; the trace is not impaired for policy purposes because none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires - coverage is 100%, there are 90 fixes at a 10-second cadence, no gaps, and a maximum gap of 10 seconds, far under the 90-second limb. No charge line lacks a counterpart in the trace or trip record. The bundle holds no traffic advisory: EV-ADVIS-00805-01 is MISSING, carries issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and has a weight_multiplier of 0.0, so its absence is citable but it can carry no fact - and because the driver asserts no external traffic cause and cites no advisory identifier, nothing is invoked against a missing artifact and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged, while POL-RD-14 confines POL-RD-10(7) to the partly-corroborated case this is not.

ruling.explanation:
The route-deviation finding rests on this trip's own instruments. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00805 measures the distance actually driven between the recorded pickup and dropoff at 5.5 km, over 90 fixes at 100% coverage and a 10-second cadence, and the booking-time platform estimate on EV-TRIP-00805 is 2.5 km over 8.0 minutes. The excess is 3.0 km, which is 120% of the optimal distance and more than 0.8 km in absolute terms, so both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass and the 50% limb is crossed as well, making the deviation material. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern; it agrees with the trip record's 5.5 km, so nothing turns on the two fields diverging. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c): it carries no gap over 90 seconds (largest gap 10 seconds), no straight-line jump over 500 m, and no sustained interval over 30 seconds. No independent corroboration is therefore needed and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation is not engaged.

The driver points to the rider's chat request, MSG-00805-001 in EV-CHAT-00805, timed 13:59:40, to stop at Golden Mile Tower first. That message meets POL-RD-04(a) to (c) - it comes from the rider, it predates departure, and it names a place - but the corroboration limb fails: the message's waypoint hint sits 1,592 m from the nearest fix on the trace, far outside the 200 m radius POL-RD-04 requires. Under POL-RD-14 that is a failed corroboration, not the mutually contradictory evidence POL-RD-10(7) describes, because a request that was made and a route that did not follow it are consistent with each other. No distance is excluded from the excess, and the driver's stated reliance on the request does not reduce it.

No traffic advisory is on file. EV-ADVIS-00805-01 is MISSING, carries issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, has a weight multiplier of 0.0 and no payload, and the trace's advisory block returns no advisories. Its absence is citable, but it can carry no fact: POL-RD-03 cannot be run and no closure exoneration is available. The driver named no advisory identifier, so nothing is invoked against a missing artifact and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged.

The material deviation triggers the POL-RD-06 profile check, which comes back negative on the clause's own test: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 300, satisfying neither the count-of-3 limb nor the 0.05 ratio limb. There is accordingly no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c). Per POL-GEN-01, prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and context only, and it was not used.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. Charged total: SGD 12.87. Recomputed fare: ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 2.5 optimal km + 0.28 x 8.0 optimal min) x 1.0 surge multiplier, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP/tolls + 0 fixed surcharges + 0 waiting time - 0 promo = SGD 8.715. Refund: SGD 4.155 before rounding, which rounds up to SGD 4.20. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and below the 90% share that would convert it to a full refund, so the outcome is a partial refund of SGD 4.20.

There is no pass-through correction. EV-FARE-00805 charges no ERP (no gantries) and no airport surcharge, and the fare model is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not run. Under POL-RD-09(1) no off-route ERP may be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. No billing-integrity referral arises. No escalation trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across EV-TRIP-00805, EV-GPS-00805 and EV-FARE-00805, the timestamps do not run backwards or diverge, the trace is unimpaired, the refund is far below the ceiling, and no exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited missing artifact.

Every artifact that carries a deciding fact here - EV-GPS-00805, EV-TRIP-00805 and EV-FARE-00805 - carries a weight multiplier of 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
